methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $9M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Infinite Machine is a seed-stage transportation company founded by Joseph Cohen and Eddie Cohen that has raised $9.3M to date. The broader transportation sector comp universe includes six private peers (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Navier, EarthGrid) and no public comparables, though these peers operate across a wide range of valuations and development stages, limiting direct peer-to-peer benchmarking.

Valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method: stage-progression analysis. Using the $9.3M total raised as a proxy for current value, application of a 2.5x multiplier—standard for seed-to-next-stage progression—yields an implied valuation of $23M. This method captures the expected value expansion between funding rounds but depends on the assumption that Infinite Machine will achieve comparable technical and commercial milestones to cohort peers.

The peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient narrow comparables at the same stage and valuation tier within Transportation. A triangulated analysis based on stage-progression results supports a valuation range of $20M (low) to $27M (high), with a median point of $23M. Primary uncertainties include the timing and terms of the next funding event, the company's progress against undisclosed technical milestones, and the extent to which sector-wide transportation venture returns will compress or expand this typical step-up multiplier.
